opening_message:

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E036.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Maurice Perez (E036) is a full-time Engineer. Requested write access to Source Code, which is at the maximum allowed level for a full-time employee. Recommending write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Maurice Perez (E036) is a contractor with basic security training (note says full-time; flagging discrepancy). Contractors with basic training max out at read. Requested write exceeds max, so recommending read.
reason: There is conflicting evidence on Maurice Perez's employment type: HR note states full-time (max write for Source Code), but the Security note states the security database shows contractor with basic security training (max read) and explicitly flags the discrepancy. Requested write access exceeds the contractor/basic-training maximum, so the maximum allowed level under the more restrictive verified record is read. Granting read avoids exceeding policy; recommending read.
